children: By Avinash  P and Ragini Mathur

Brazilian stocks and the real rose on Tuesday after a new poll showed improved prospects for right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro in next month's presidential election, while higher commodity prices lifted assets across Latin America.
A Nexus poll commissioned by BTG Pactual showed Bolsonaro holding a narrow lead over left-wing President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in a simulated second-round runoff for next month's election.

Brazil's first-round vote is scheduled for October 4, with a runoff, if required, set for October 25. Recent polls have shown Bolsonaro steadily narrowing the gap with Lula, keeping the election outcome at the center of investors' focus amid concerns over deteriorating public finances.
Investors broadly view Bolsonaro as the more market-friendly candidate. The benchmark Bovespa

"There is some still political risk in Brazil, but it has very high carry and strong commodities. Those two, mostly dominated in terms of just attracting investor capital into these markets," said Lale Akoner, global market strategist at eToro.
"Much of the macro drivers are aligning well in terms of boosting these markets right now."
The broader MSCI index index tracking LatAm equities (.MILA00000PUS) rose 1.4%, while the regional FX index (.MILA00000CUS) gained 0.5%

Oil, an important export for several Latin American economies, held near six-week highs after Iran-backed Houthi forces attacked Saudi energy facilities. The attacks heightened concerns that a wider conflict in the Gulf could disrupt global fuel supplies.
In Chile, stocks (.MICL00000PUS) rose 0.4%, following copper prices to record highs. The country is the world's largest copper producer. The peso
appreciated 1% to a near two-week high.

Data showed Chilean consumer prices rose 0.6% in August from the previous month, pushing annual inflation to 4.1% from 3.5% in July and above the central bank's 2%-4% target range. Investors awaited the central bank's rate decision later in the day, with policymakers widely expected to keep rates unchanged at 4.5%.
Peru's stock index (.MXNUAMPESCPGPE), also supported by higher copper prices, added 0.7%.

In Colombia, consumer prices rose 0.39% in August, data showed on Monday, taking annual price growth to 6.24%, which remains well above the central bank's target range of 3% plus or minus one percentage point.

"The recent patch of soft inflation in Mexico is unlikely to be sustained," said Kimberley Sperrfechter, senior emerging markets economist at Capital Economics.
"With Banxico likely to raise its inflation forecasts substantially as the Fed shifts toward rate hikes, the balance of probabilities is tilted toward further monetary tightening in Mexico."
Key Latin American stock indexes and currencies at 1945 GMT:
LatAm stocks climb 1.4%, currency index gains 0.5%
Poll suggests Brazil's Bolsonaro would beat Lula by one point in a runoff
Chile's consumer prices rise more than expected in August
Chile's central bank decision due later in the day
Colombia 12-month inflation edges above expectations in August
